records.text:
今天股市新闻：

1. 2026年第三季度财报季拉开帷幕，摩根大通 $JPM、高盛 $GS、花旗集团 $C 和富国银行 $WFC 发布了报告，为银行业呈现出一幅喜忧参半但总体韧性十足的图景。高盛领跑该集团，录得有史以来第二佳季度收入，权益交易激增72%；花旗集团报告称，其十年来的最佳第三季度得益于服务、财富管理和权益业务的强劲表现。摩根大通尽管上调了2026年净利息收入展望，但仍罕见地出现财报不及预期；富国银行财报超预期，但收入不及预期。整个行业中，银行继续将美国消费者描述为韧性十足，强调持续的AI驱动企业投资，上调或维持乐观的净利息收入预期，并指出权益交易活动强劲，同时警告称，顽固通胀、更长时间维持高利率、高估值以及地缘政治风险仍是进入2027年的关键挑战。

2. 美国银行表示，根据其最新全球基金经理调查，10年期美国国债收益率可能需要接近6%，投资者才会大规模从股票转向债券。该调查发现，76%的受访者预计美联储将在10月维持利率不变，同时科技股配置攀升至2020年8月以来的最高水平，长线半导体仍是市场最拥挤的交易。与此同时，非必需消费品敞口降至2008年7月以来的最低水平，投资者增加对债券、公用事业、日本和英国的配置，同时削减对银行和美国权益的敞口。美国银行表示，整体权益情绪仍具韧性，但债券收益率的无序上升以及AI泡沫的潜在风险如今被视为市场面临的最大风险。

3. 保罗·都铎·琼斯警告称，2027年可能成为“市场非常具有挑战性的一年”，称当前状况让他“完全想起了1999年”。他认为市场短期内可能继续表现良好，但相信长期风险正在积累，并指出许多投资者此前未经历过类似周期。琼斯还表示，他预计将在2027年全年保持空头头寸，认为估值几乎毫无价值，并将之与1998–2002年时期相类比，当时大量IPO发行和内部人士股份解锁不断增加市场供给，创造了他描述的维持空头头寸的最轻松环境之一。

4. 苹果 $AAPL 在今天的“Welcome Home”活动中发布了HomeView，这是其首款专用智能家居中枢，标志着自HomeKit以来公司最大的智能家居扩展。这款299美元设备配备7英寸Liquid Retina显示屏、Siri AI、支持最多6位用户的Face ID、FaceTime、Matter和Thread兼容性，以及对摄像头、锁、灯、恒温器和其他智能家居设备的集中控制，目前已开放预订和发货。苹果还推出了HomePod mini 2（149美元）、全新Apple TV 4K（299美元），以及与LG和施耐德电气合作开发的Apple Home Collection智能家居配件系列，包括摄像头、视频门铃、智能锁、恒温器和传感器。这些公告代表苹果迄今为止对联网家居最具侵略性的推进，将公司定位为更直接地与亚马逊Echo和谷歌Nest竞争，同时强调隐私、本设备智能和深度生态系统整合。

5. 甲骨文 $ORCL 敦促联邦监管机构加快批准Green Chile天然气管道项目，称该项目对按计划推进其在新墨西哥州庞大的Project Jupiter AI数据中心建设至关重要。在致FERC的一封信中，甲骨文高级副总裁乔什·皮特科克表示，进一步延误可能危及项目时间表，以及相关的就业、经济活动和社区利益。由Energy Transfer拥有的管道预计将每天向为Project Jupiter提供动力的Bloom Energy燃料电池供应约4亿立方英尺天然气，但投产时间已从原定的8月15日推迟至2027年2月。

6. OpenAI表示，其在一间办公室内发现了一个精密录音设备，据称是几天前一名员工安装的。公司表示，该员工已被解雇，此事已移交FBI。根据OpenAI的说法，没有证据显示该个人不当访问或窃取了模型权重、源代码或客户数据。这一事件凸显了随着AI公司保护日益宝贵的知识产权，物理和运营安全的重要性日益增加。

7. NVIDIA $NVDA 首席执行官黄仁勋表示，公司将于下周宣布额外20亿美元在欧洲的投资，从而使NVIDIA过去一年的区域投资总额达到约100亿美元。黄仁勋计划访问伦敦和柏林，还宣布了对四家法国AI初创公司的全新投资：Doctolib、Genesis AI、Pigment和Entalpic。针对AI安全和数据中心能耗担忧，黄仁勋辩称AI可以安全开发，同时推动经济增长，反对放缓AI开发，并表示开源模型可以通过实现语言和行业特定定制，帮助欧洲缩小与美国的AI差距。他敦促欧洲在全球竞争加剧之际加速AI投资和创新努力。

8. 今日交易量最大的10只期权（按合约数量计）为：$NVDA 170万份合约、$AAPL 120万份合约、$MU 100万份合约、$META 97.5万份合约、$SPCX 97.1万份合约、$TSLA 91.1万份合约、$INTC 79.2万份合约、$MSFT 50.7万份合约、$AMZN 49.6万份合约，以及$AMD 48.9万份合约。

9. 最新的ADP全国就业报告显示，在截至9月26日的四周内，美国私营雇主平均每周新增24,750个就业岗位，低于此前的25,250周平均水平，标志着连续五周就业改善的结束。最新读数代表周就业创造量下降2%，尽管招聘仍远高于7月底录得的8,250周平均水平。这一温和的招聘趋势可能指向劳动力市场逐步降温，有望随着时间推移缓解工资压力和通胀。

records.text:
この記事は、昨日のロイターの記事（米国の貿易赤字が過去最高）への、一つの「答え」になっている記事だと思います。

■数字の整理
・日本の対米投融資の枠　5,500億ドル（約87兆円）
・これまでに決まった額　1,090億ドル（計画の約2割）
・まだ使われていない枠　約4,400億ドル
・今回の半導体工場　事業規模2兆円ほど、運営はグローバルファウンドリーズ

■本質は「工場は米国に、注文は日本に」
トランプ政権は、貿易赤字を減らすために「米国で作れ」と言っています。今回の工場はまさにその形です。ただ、工場の中に並ぶ製造装置は、記事のとおり日本企業が担います。建物は米国に建っても、その中身の注文は日本の装置会社に流れる。
もう一つ大事なのは、昨日お伝えした「関税の蛇口」との関係です。中間選挙の前後で、トランプ政権がアジアの半導体に厳しくなる可能性がありますが、日本はこの5,500億ドルの約束で、米国にとって「投資してくれる相手」という立場を作っています。関税の圧力が強まった時、真っ先に狙われるのは巨額の黒字を積み上げている韓国と台湾で、日本は相対的に守られやすい。これは日本の半導体株にとって見えにくい保険です。

■どの会社に流れるか
一つ押さえておきたいのは、グローバルファウンドリーズは最先端の微細化競争から2018年に降りた会社だということです。
最先端用のEUV露光装置は基本的に使いません。ですから、恩恵はEUVの周辺（レーザーテックなど）より、汎用の製造装置と材料の会社に流れます。
・東京エレクトロン（8035）　成膜・エッチング・塗布現像と、工場に一番多く並ぶ装置を持つ
・SCREENホールディングス（7735）　洗浄装置の世界最大手
・KOKUSAI ELECTRIC（6525）　成膜装置
・荏原製作所（6361）　ウエハーを平らに磨く装置
・信越化学工業（4063）　シリコンウエハーの世界最大手
ただ、2兆円の工場1つで、これらの会社の業績が大きく変わるわけではありません。東京エレクトロン1社の営業利益が年1兆円規模ですから、1件の効果は限られます。

■本当の意味は「残りの4,400億ドル」
大事なのは、今回の1件ではなく、この先に約4,400億ドルの枠が残っていることです。赤沢経産相は、これからの案件は「AIと半導体の比重が非常に大きくなる」と述べています。第1弾、第2弾はガス火力やSMRといった電力、第3弾から半導体。
つまり、今後も数カ月おきに、日本の装置会社や電力・原発関連が潤う案件が発表されていく可能性が高い。文明投資OSの中期枠の「二の組」と、第3の層の原発関連（日本製鋼所など）の両方にとって、繰り返し訪れる追い風の材料になります。

■まとめ
対米投融資は、「米国に工場を建てて、日本に注文が来る」仕組みであり、関税の圧力から日本を守る保険でもあります。1件ごとの効果は小さくても、残り4,400億ドルの案件が、AI半導体と電力に向けて続いていく。文明投資OSの中期枠で東京エレクトロンを軸に置く理由が、もう一つ増えたと思います。

（10月15日）

1. 主要指数終値

2. 前営業日の米国市場概況

10月14日のNY市場は、米消費者物価指数（CPI）の上振れを受けて追加利上げへの警戒が強まり、AI・半導体株を中心に売りが広がりました。 

9月CPIは前年同月比3.7％上昇と、8月の3.4％から加速し、市場予想の3.6％も上回りました。中東情勢の緊迫化による燃料価格の上昇が物価を押し上げています。

米10年債利回りは一時5.32％を突破。FRBの10月利上げ確率も前日の22％から約35％へ上昇し、高金利長期化への懸念が強まりました。

個別では、エヌビディアが3.2％安、ブロードコムが3.1％安、AMDが5.7％安。

金利上昇によってAIデータセンターの資金調達コストが膨らむとの懸念が売りにつながりました。AIクラウドのコアウィーブは15.5％急落し、オラクルも8.8％下落。

銀行株では、バンク・オブ・アメリカが4.8％安。決算が市場予想を下回ったうえ、約12億ドルの制裁金も嫌気されました。ステート・ストリートも4.1％下落。

インフレ再燃とAI投資の収益性への懸念が重なり、成長株への売り圧力が強まる展開となりました。

3. 東京市場の見通し

15日の東京株式市場は、米国のインフレ再加速とAI・半導体株の大幅下落を受け、売り先行の展開となりそうです。

14日発表の米9月消費者物価指数（CPI）は前年同月比3.7％上昇し、8月の3.4％から加速。エネルギー価格の高騰が主因で、食品・エネルギーを除くコア指数も2.6％上昇しました。

米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）の追加利上げ観測が強まり、金利上昇に弱い成長株への売り圧力が高まっています。

シカゴの日経平均先物も大きく下落しており、東京市場では下値を探る展開が警戒されます。

14日に決算を発表したオランダのASMLは、7～9月期売上高が116億6200万ユーロとなり、AI向け需要の拡大を背景に2027～28年は供給能力が需要に追いつかない可能性を示しました。

本日15時には台湾TSMCの決算説明会が予定されており、AI半導体の需要見通しと設備投資計画が市場の方向性を左右する重要材料となりそうです。

個別では良品計画に注目です。14日に発表した2026年8月期決算は営業利益が40.1％増の1034億円となり、初めて1000億円を突破。今期も10.2％増益を見込み、好業績を評価する買いが期待されます。

サイゼリヤも今期経常利益を23.6％増と予想し、4期連続の最高益更新を見込んでいます。

一方、米金融株安を受け、三菱UFJフィナンシャル・グループ、三井住友フィナンシャルグループなど銀行株への影響も警戒されます。

本日は国内の機械受注統計に加え、米国でも生産者物価指数（PPI）や小売売上高の発表が予定されています。

東京市場は半導体株の下げ止まりを見極めながら、好決算の内需株へ資金が向かうかが焦点となりそうです。

长文预警：35B MoE 多模态 AI，跑在手机上，只要 3GB 内存？MiniCPM-V 4.7 + LES这是面壁智能的解法。今天把 LES（Lookahead Expert Scheduling，前瞻专家调度）一次讲透，也讲清它和 Strata 这类 PC 端推理框架到底差在哪。👇

1. LES 是什么？

LES 是面壁智能为 MiniCPM-V 4.7 研发的 MoE 推理加速技术。目标很直接：让 35B-A3B 的 MoE 多模态模型在手机、iOS、Android 上本地跑起来，内存约 3GB，还能读真实路牌、规划约束、解析复杂文档、推理视觉数据。轻量 1B 变体则覆盖资源更紧的硬件。

一句话：它让“35B MoE multimodal AI. On your phone. With just 3GB of memory.”从口号变成可运行现实。

2. 为什么 MoE 在端侧会卡？

MoE 像一支专家团队，每次只激活少数专家。但传统方式是“按需加载”：用到哪个专家，才把它从存储搬进内存，算完再搬走。

问题来了：这种“一搬一停”会造成频繁 I/O 等待，计算被反复打断，生成速度一顿一顿。这就是端侧 MoE 最要命的“内存墙”。

3. LES 的答案：预测式预加载

核心思想：提前预判，边跑边接棒。让专家权重的加载与模型计算并行，而不是串行等待。

关键观察：大模型相邻层的输入特征高度相似，所以下一层需要哪些专家，是可以被提前预测的。

工作流程：

  第 L 层计算还没结束，就用第 L 层输出隐藏状态，结合第 L+1 层路由门权重，预测下一层最可能被选中的 top-k 专家，比如 8 个。
  预测不干预真实路由，只是预判。
  预测出的专家 ID 交给后台 I/O 线程池，用 os.pread 从 SSD 异步预读权重。
  读取窗口正好藏在当前层 GPU 计算时间里。命中，下一层专家已在内存；失败，也无损回退到按需读取，主路径不阻塞。

 官方数据显示：预测下一层 8 个专家，命中率超过 80%。预测窗口约 1.15ms，也就是 1 个 token 的解码时间，足够后台完成预读。

 开源社区实测：引入 LES 风格预取后，冷缓存场景速度提升 17%，热缓存场景提升 23%，稳态下磁盘读取量减少约 0.57GB/请求。

4. LES 不是单打独斗

它和 MiniCPM-V 4.7 的其他技术协同作战：

  层-wise 量化：把权重压到 4-bit 甚至更低，大幅降低内存占用；LES 负责高效搬运这些量化权重。
  DSpark 推测采样：35B 版本配一个 389M 参数的草稿模型，先“猜”后续多个 token，再由大模型并行验证；LES 提前准备好所需专家，进一步加速。
  SRFT，Self-Replay Fine-Tuning：开发者可以针对新任务定制模型，同时维持通用性能。
  1B 轻量变体：在资源受限硬件上也能完成多模态理解。

5. 性能表现

  iPhone 17 Pro Max：约 3GB 内存，13+ token/s。
  iPad Pro M4：超过 15 token/s。
  端侧推理速度提升约 5 倍。
  从 iOS 到 Android，MiniCPM-V 4.7 让强大多模态 AI 更 practical 地本地运行。

本质上，LES 是一个低开销“预取器”。它利用模型自身层间的可预测性，把“等待 + 串行加载”换成“预测 + 并行加载”，突破 MoE 在端侧部署时最关键的 I/O 瓶颈。

6. 那和 Strata 这类 PC 端推理框架有什么区别？

目标相似：都是在有限硬件上跑大模型。但设计哲学、核心机制、适用场景，根本不同。

① 设计哲学

  LES：模型内生的端侧优化方案。目标是让 35B 的 MiniCPM-V 4.7 在手机上以“无损”方式流畅运行，核心指标是极低内存约 3GB、无感卡顿、能效比、极致轻量。不依赖硬件堆叠。
  Strata：系统级的 PC 端推理引擎。目标是让 125B 级 Qwen 类模型在消费级 PC 上运行，核心指标是高吞吐、低硬件门槛，比如 12GB 显存。它把 SSD、RAM、VRAM、CPU 都变成推理流水线。

② 核心机制

  LES：预测路由，提前预取。利用 MoE 相邻层输入特征高度相似，在当前层计算时预测下一层可能激活的专家。后台异步预读，计算与加载并行。预测不干预真实路由，命中率超 80%，失败无损回退。
  Strata：三级缓存 + 投机解码。高频专家放 VRAM，低频专家放 RAM，甚至用 SSD 存 n-gram 表。通过自适应算法动态学习哪些专家“最热”，命中率可从 92.7% 爬升到 99.1%。再用轻量草稿模型 MTP 一次预测多个 token，由大模型并行验证，实现 1.6-1.8 倍额外加速。

③ 技术实现与性能

  LES：与层-wise 量化、DSpark 推测采样协同。iPhone 上约 3GB 内存，13+ token/s；iPad Pro M4 超 15 token/s；端侧推理速度提升约 5 倍。
  Strata：支持双 GPU 流水线，RTX 5080 + 4060 Ti 可达 143 tok/s；--layer-split 模式让两张卡同时工作，避免资源闲置。RTX 5070 12GB 上，125B 模型可达 94 token/s。

④ 适用场景

  LES：手机、平板、资源极度受限设备。追求能效比、轻量、本地多模态。
  Strata：消费级 PC、多 GPU 工作站。追求极限吞吐、硬件利用率，挑战服务器级模型速度。

LES 像“精算师”：深入模型内部，利用模型自身的可预测性，用极低额外开销四两拨千斤。目标是让手机这种资源极度受限的设备也能跑动大模型，追求能效比和极致轻量。

Strata 像“总调度”：站在系统层面，把 PC 的 SSD、RAM、VRAM、CPU/GPU 全部纳入统一调度，用复杂缓存策略和投机解码大力出奇迹。目标是让消费级 PC 挑战服务器级模型的吞吐量，追求极限性能和硬件利用率。

两者不是竞争关系，他们各自针对不同硬件形态和用户需求给出了不同的解答方案。

MiniCPM-V 4.7 的意义在于：35B MoE 多模态、手机 3GB、iOS/Android、SRFT 可定制、1B 轻量版。端侧 AI 不再只是“小模型玩具”，开始真正实用起来了。

#MiniCPM #LES #MoE #OnDeviceAI #多模态 #Strata #端侧AI

🚨🚨🚨 $XRP holders, listen closely to what the IMF is discussing: gold reserves, foreign-currency liquidity, and a financial problem XRP is already built to compete in.

Long read ahead, but trust me, this one is worth your time.

I went through the IMF discussion with Calixto José Ortega Sánchez, Venezuela’s Vice President for the Economy and former president of the country’s central bank, and I don’t think people should listen to this as another conversation about gold prices.

He is talking about something much deeper.

-International reserves.
-Foreign-currency access.
-Central-bank swap lines.
-Gold production.
-Gold held by the central bank.

All of those subjects come back to the same basic problem every country eventually faces: it can own valuable reserve assets, but when the financial system actually needs dollars, foreign currency, collateral or settlement liquidity, that value has to become usable.

That is the part I keep thinking about as an $XRP holder.

Gold can stay in a vault.

A government can keep the reserve.

A bank can keep the financial asset.

But the moment somebody needs to exchange the value represented by that asset into another form of money, finance becomes a liquidity problem.

And the world is increasingly trying to solve that liquidity problem digitally.

The IMF itself published research in 2026 that lines up with exactly what I’m studying.

One side of the research deals with gold inside central-bank reserves: custody, reserve management and the challenge of converting gold into foreign-currency liquidity when that liquidity is needed.

Then Tobias Adrian, Director of the IMF’s Monetary and Capital Markets Department, separately discussed how tokenization can move asset ownership, payments and settlement onto programmable ledgers.

Those are two different subjects, but I see them moving toward the same future.

Reserve assets remain important.

The infrastructure surrounding those assets becomes digital.

Ownership becomes easier to represent electronically.

Collateral becomes easier to administer.

Settlement becomes programmable.

And financial institutions need liquid markets connecting all of those different forms of value.

Now look at Venezuela itself.

A particularly important development appeared in September 2026 involving approximately $4 billion of disputed Venezuelan gold held at the Bank of England.

Under the reported proposal, that gold could potentially be moved to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York and used as collateral to obtain financing rather than simply being sold.

Think about what that tells us about reserve assets.

The gold does not necessarily have to leave the financial system through a sale.

It can remain valuable collateral.

The holder can try to unlock liquidity against it.

That is exactly the kind of financial function I expect tokenization to make easier to administer over time.

Imagine a legally recognized structure where physical gold remains with an approved custodian.

A regulated issuer creates a digital claim representing rights against that gold.

That digital claim enters a financial market.

It can potentially be pledged as collateral.

A lender provides digital dollars or another eligible currency.

The collateral position and financing can then be tracked, transferred or settled using digital infrastructure.

The gold itself never needs to become XRP.

The gold does not need to be “backing XRP.”

The opportunity I’m interested in sits in the exchange layer surrounding the asset.

If the gold-linked claim needs to trade against dollars, tokenized deposits, securities or national currencies, somebody has to provide liquidity between those markets.

That is where XRP starts becoming very interesting to me.

Because XRPL already has the ability to issue and exchange tokenized assets.

And gold-linked assets are already appearing in that ecosystem.

Assetiko Commodities publishes documentation for XAUa, a gold-linked product issued on XRPL and Stellar.

Its documentation says one XAUa represents exposure equivalent to one fine troy ounce of gold.

Its reserve structure can include physical gold, gold ETFs, certificates and cash equivalents, with redemption arrangements and an XRPL issuer address.

That is a concrete example of gold exposure being represented through the type of infrastructure I’m talking about.

Then there is Meld Gold.

Its model connects miners, refiners, vault operators and users through digitally represented precious metals, and founder Michael Cotton has participated in XRP Ledger ecosystem events.

Its XRPL deployment is still developing, but the direction matters to me because it shows another company working on precious-metal tokenization around the XRP Ledger ecosystem.

Zoom out from XRPL and the market becomes even more interesting.

The broader tokenized-gold market had already approached $6 billion in February 2026, led by products such as Tether Gold and Paxos Gold.

So this is not an industry waiting to be invented.

People already want digital exposure to gold.

Products already exist.

Capital is already there.

My question is what happens when those products become more deeply integrated into collateral, settlement and professional trading markets.

That leads directly into one of the strongest technical parts of my XRP thesis:

XRPL auto-bridging.

XRP Ledger has supported XRP auto-bridging since 2014.

The system can use XRP as an intermediary when two issued assets can exchange more efficiently by routing through XRP liquidity.

That matters a lot once a financial network has many different tokenized assets.

Because every asset cannot have equally deep direct liquidity against every other asset.

Imagine a regulated gold token.

An institution already holds RLUSD.

It wants the gold-linked asset.

The direct RLUSD/gold-token market might be thin.

XRPL can look at competing liquidity and potentially use XRP between the two assets when that route gives a better exchange.

The flow becomes:

RLUSD → XRP → tokenized gold.

Now XRP is sitting between digital dollars and gold exposure.

The same mechanism can potentially work across many other issued assets and currencies.

And once professional market makers start supporting those markets, they need inventory.

That inventory angle is one of the most important parts of my entire XRP thesis.

A market maker cannot continuously quote XRP markets using imaginary capital.

If a professional firm provides XRP/gold-token liquidity, it may need XRP.

If it also provides RLUSD/XRP liquidity, it needs capital on that side too.

If it supports several currencies and tokenized assets, the same XRP inventory can help service multiple markets.

So XRP becomes working capital.

It is sitting there because somebody needs it to run the market.

That is a completely different demand profile from someone buying XRP only because they expect the price to rise.

A professional trading firm may need XRP because customers want liquidity.

And the deeper the institutional market becomes, the more important that working inventory can become.

Then I started looking at collateral infrastructure around Ripple itself.

Ripple invested in ZILO and Licuido to expand digital transfer agency, issuance and collateral-mobility capabilities.

Then Standard Chartered announced live institutional custody for XRPL-issued RLUSD.

Standard Chartered is also involved with Ripple and LMAX Group in a planned arrangement where RLUSD can be recognized as trading collateral.

Again, I’m looking at the machinery.

Custody.

Issuance.

Collateral.

Digital cash.

Liquidity.

Settlement.

The individual products may be different, but the financial functions keep moving in the same direction.

Now think about a future institution that holds a tokenized gold-backed financial asset and digital dollars at the same time.

The tokenized gold could potentially serve as collateral.

The institution borrows or settles in digital dollars.

XRP liquidity can sit between eligible markets when professional participants choose XRP routes.

That creates a structure I keep coming back to:

Gold as reserve or collateral → digital dollars as financing → XRP as exchange liquidity.

I like this scenario because XRP does not need to replace gold.

It does not need to replace national currencies.

It does not need every bank to throw away its existing balance sheet.

It only needs to become useful between markets that already exist.

And finance has a lot of markets that need to talk to each other.

Now look at what the IMF has been discussing in its own tokenization work.

Tokenized bank deposits.

Stablecoins.

Tokenized central-bank money.

Cross-border settlement.

Collateral management.

Atomic exchange between assets and payments.

These are not random crypto buzzwords coming from a small startup.

These are financial workflows the IMF is examining as part of the modernization of financial architecture.

Then compare those workflows with the XRP Ledger ecosystem.

Digital representation of assets can use XRPL tokenization infrastructure.

Cross-currency exchange can use the native DEX and auto-bridging.

Digital-dollar settlement can involve RLUSD.

Regulated trading can use permissioned markets.

Institutional asset custody connects through Ripple Custody and external custodians.

And XRP can become intermediary liquidity when market participants actually choose XRP-denominated routes.

That is the overlap I’m watching.

I am not claiming the IMF selected XRP.

I don’t need that claim to see the opportunity.

The important part is that global finance is moving toward workflows where XRP already has technology designed to compete.

Then the Bank for International Settlements gives us another serious example.

Project Agorá demonstrated atomic cross-border settlement involving tokenized commercial-bank deposits and central-bank reserves.

The project included major central banks and more than 40 private financial institutions.

It showed how multicurrency transactions can be settled across connected institutional systems.

The BIS also announced plans to move toward testing involving real value.

I keep coming back to that word: connected.

Because tokenizing one asset is only the first step.

Financial institutions then need those assets to interact.

They need to move from one currency to another.

They need collateral to support financing.

They need securities to exchange against cash.

They need cross-border liquidity.

They need markets that can operate around different asset types.

That is why I care so much about the liquidity layer.

Project Agorá itself is centered on central-bank reserves and commercial-bank deposits, but the modernization around it creates adjacent commercial markets.

Those adjacent markets are places where XRP can compete as intermediary liquidity.

Then Venezuela adds another interesting reserve-management piece.

In April 2026, the IMF resumed institutional engagement with Venezuela and confirmed that the country could again access its Special Drawing Rights holdings and IMF reserve position, together worth roughly $4.9 billion at the time.

Now look at how many forms of reserve value are involved in one country’s situation.

Monetary gold.

Foreign currencies.

SDRs.

IMF reserve assets.

Swap-line access.

Collateral.

Financing.

They are different assets serving different jobs.

A modern financial system needs infrastructure capable of managing and exchanging those forms of value when institutions need liquidity.

As more claims become digital, I expect the value of multi-asset settlement infrastructure to keep rising.

And while all of this is being discussed at the institutional level, Ripple is expanding deeper into exactly the areas surrounding tokenized financial markets.

On October 14, Ripple and Meritz Securities announced a strategic partnership around digital-asset custody and tokenization for South Korea’s capital markets.

Meritz became Ripple’s fourth announced institutional partner in Korea during 2026.

The other names identified by Ripple include Kyobo Life Insurance, Kbank and Jeonbuk Bank.

Then widen the map.

Standard Chartered has live XRPL-issued RLUSD custody and the planned LMAX collateral arrangement.

BNY is the primary custodian of RLUSD reserves.

Guggenheim Treasury Services has digital commercial paper on XRPL.

CSD BR and BTG Pactual are connected to XRPL securities-recording infrastructure.

Mercado Bitcoin announced a $200 million regulated-asset tokenization initiative on XRPL.

Aviva Investors is exploring tokenized funds.

Different institutions.

Different countries.

Different financial products.

But custody, issuance, tokenization, digital cash, collateral and settlement are starting to live inside the same broader institutional conversation.

That is why I keep separating XRP’s real price mechanism from the size of the assets being tokenized.

If an institution tokenizes $1 billion of gold, it does not automatically mean $1 billion of XRP gets purchased.

I’m interested in something more realistic and potentially much more powerful over time:

How much XRP do institutions need to maintain to keep those markets liquid?

The research models an illustrative situation with 10× daily inventory turnover.

At $100 million of XRP-routed gold or FX trading per day, roughly $10 million of XRP inventory could support that activity.

At $500 million, roughly $50 million.

At $1 billion, about $100 million.

At $5 billion, around $500 million.

At $10 billion, approximately $1 billion of working inventory.

Those numbers are scenarios.

The bigger lesson is what matters to me.

Recurring financial activity creates a reason to maintain capital.

The XRP can come through spot purchases.

It can come through borrowing.

It can be financed.

But somebody still needs access to the token if the market depends on XRP liquidity.

And if several tokenized markets develop independently, the combined professional inventory requirement can start becoming meaningful.

That is the long-term XRP price mechanism I keep studying.

Gold/XRP markets can create inventory demand.

XRP-mediated FX conversion can create intermediary demand.

Eligible XRP collateral can lock tokens into financial positions.

Institutional accumulation can create operating balances.

XRPL transactions burn XRP fees.

Ledger accounts and qualifying objects require XRP reserves.

The current base account reserve is 1 XRP, with an additional 0.2 XRP for most qualifying ledger objects.

The fees themselves are small, so I care much more about professional liquidity and long-term institutional holdings than a tiny transaction-fee narrative.

From everything I went through, I see five bullish developments worth tracking very closely.

Tokenized gold becoming an actively traded and financed asset class.

Banks creating more ways to mobilize tokenized collateral.

RLUSD liquidity becoming increasingly connected to tokenized assets.

Regulated institutions deepening their XRPL integrations.

And professional market makers maintaining larger XRP inventories as institutional flows increase.

My 2027–2030 scenario grows from there.

In 2027, I expect more regulated financial providers to explore digital claims linked to physical precious metals.

The existing tokenized-gold market already gives the industry a commercial model.

XRPL can compete as one of the networks supporting those products.

By 2028, I expect some gold-linked assets to move beyond simple buy-and-hold exposure and become more useful in financing and collateral arrangements.

The physical metal can remain with qualified custodians.

The financial claim becomes easier to administer digitally.

Digital dollars can provide the cash side.

XRP can compete for trading, currency conversion and liquidity surrounding those markets.

Then by 2029–2030, I see financial institutions operating increasingly interconnected markets containing tokenized securities, bank deposits, stablecoins and precious-metals exposure.

Every one of those markets needs liquidity.

Every asset cannot maintain deep direct markets against every other asset.

A common intermediary becomes valuable.

If XRP becomes one of the preferred assets used between those markets, professional institutions will need to hold it because their financial operations require it.

That is the future I’m watching.

Not “XRP will replace gold.”

Not “the IMF is secretly adopting XRP.”

I think the more powerful thesis is much simpler.

Gold remains gold.

Currencies remain currencies.

Banks continue managing assets.

Tokenized securities expand.

Digital dollars expand.

The world becomes more programmable.

And all those assets still need markets where value can move between them.

XRP was designed to compete inside that liquidity problem.

XRPL already has issued assets.

It already has a native DEX.

It already has auto-bridging.

RLUSD gives the ecosystem a regulated digital-dollar leg.

Ripple is expanding institutional custody, collateral, tokenization and capital-market relationships around the world.

The global institutions themselves are openly researching programmable settlement, tokenized deposits, collateral and digital money.

That combination gives me one of the strongest long-term XRP scenarios I’ve studied.

The three things I’ll keep following most closely are growing XRP liquidity against gold tokens and stablecoins, larger XRP balances maintained by professional market makers, and actual institutional use of XRP as bridge liquidity or eligible collateral.

Those are the receipts that would show the thesis moving from infrastructure into real token demand.

The day banks and market makers need XRP to keep these markets running, people will finally understand what this asset was built for.

Respectfully disagree

It was over long before 2019.  The rel val sheet below is from the first week of 2016.  

CHK and CRC bonds were trading in the 30s and didn't file for bankruptcy for 4 more years.  People forget how much room HY bonds give issuers to extend and pretend.  Even with much smaller equity cushions than many of the AI names.  

CRK bonds were trading at $16 with 50% yield and they never filed, nor did a few others that traded at distressed levels

Indeed from early Feb 2016 to the end of the 2016, high yield energy bonds returned 50%....oil caught a bottom and the fear was time to buy..... but 2016 to 2019 was just a slog with continued bankrupticies until covid put final nail in coffin in 2020.

E&Ps typically funded the borrowing base revolver then termed out in the bond market.  Rinse and repeat.  Banks would lend against PUDs at 50% but typically there were other limiting requirements that reduced that further and you were typically +/- 2x covered.  

Shale was a natty gas phenomena to start and in the first few years..... the Permian was one of last shale basins to get going.  Producers chased gas early, overproduced, crushed the price, then chased liquids/oil later and did the same thing so was a rolling crash for many years.  I remember getting bearish gas as early as 2009 and stayed that way for well over a decade.  You could just run the math and see demand could not match supply growth.  The shale implosion was a s/d mismatch and ensuing price drop as much as a leverage issue.

A100 rental prices (NVDA 2020 chips / 6 years oold) are up this year as are every other generation of chips despite newer, more efficient chips entering service.  Demand is greater than supply currently.  CRWV has said they signed a 2029 take or pay contract on A100s this year, so they will run 9 years.  GPUs have been used for years for machine learning before AI.  What you see, what you get fed at sites custom to your preferences and history has been done by ML for many years, GPUs arent some new chips that are being used for the first time.  AMZN shortened to 5 yrs last year.  META extended to 6 years.  But we dont know GPU specific.  NBIS went from 4 to 5 as a GPU pure play.  Six year old A100s are appreciating assets this year.  

Token growth is outpacing token per watt growth and model efficiencies.  Until that changes materially, there is very little room for replacing older chips.  Further, in a few years the installed capacity will make that concept mathematically impossible because of chip production and power constraints.  Newer chips reduce token per watt, but we need lower token pricing to see widespread adoption imo.  The vast majority of the power additions in the US the last five years were solar/wind/battery.  We can't just flip a switch and build only gas plants like the admin wants.  Nukes will take many years.  Power will be a limiting factor for supply.  As the installed capacity grows it will be increasingly harder to 'replace' a material part of said capacity because of power and production constraints.

A small oversupply in oil & gas markets can lead to big price drops.   It was quite easy to see the oversupply coming from shale.  And quite easy to predict demand, which doesnt move much.  I started raising for a short energy credit fund in 2014.  Was short CHK in size years before based on gas price view.    

Anthropic forecast 10x token growth this year.  GOOGL reported 7x May 2025 to May 2026.  Enterprise demand is just starting imo.  Agentic tokens have surpassed human token usage, something nobody saw coming a year ago.  Normies are barely using AI yet. 

There is nothing easy about forecasting demand nor supply with AI currently..... nobody really knows when supply meets demand.  There are similarities of course, huge amounts of capital being raised for a capital intensive business with uncertain ROIC.  But increasing supply into a market that grows at population growth +/- is far different than increasing supply in a market 5-10x'ing annually.  

2016-2020 when energy really imploded, the market shrugged off and rest of market was fine.  Breadth been horrible this year, housing, software, etc imploding.  We have a shitty war with no end in sight, increasing inflation, rates rising, election uncertainty.  Is it the end of the AI trade?  Maybe.  My crystal ball was quite clear with energy trade.  I dont have any clarity currently and still think we are early in adoption cycle, meaning demand continues to outpace supply for a few years.

我跟着 Nathan Lambert 开源的 tracked-models 列表，自己拉了一遍 Hugging Face 的下载数据，想验证他那句「算上本地量化版，开源模型下载其实没在掉」。

先说背景：很多人不下原版模型，而是下别人做好的「本地版」，比如 GGUF（llama.cpp、Ollama 用的格式）、MLX（Mac 上跑的）、AWQ 这类压缩过的权重。只盯着原版仓库的下载数，这部分人就全漏了。

我做的事：他的列表里有 1606 个本地版仓库，对应 432 个原版模型。我用 HF 的公开接口把最近 30 天的下载数全拉了下来（原版只有 1 个没拉到），按原版的参数量分组，算「本地版下载占总下载的比例」。

发现了三件事：
1. 整体 36% 的下载走的是本地版。2026 年发布的模型，这个比例到了 52%，去掉 Qwen3.8-27B 这个超级大户也还有 42%；2024、2025 年的模型只有 23% 到 26%。新模型只看原版下载，会被严重低估。
2. 「模型越大，越多人用量化版」只对了一半。10B 到 150B 这一段是 58%，小于 10B 和大于 150B 的两头都只有 21% 左右。DeepSeek-V3.2 原版 30 天 478 万次下载，本地版加起来才 2800 次。
3. 本地下载里 GGUF 占 45%，MLX 19%，AWQ 14%，GPTQ 和 bitsandbytes 已经很边缘了。而且 83% 的本地下载来自 unsloth、lmstudio 这类第三方，不是模型官方自己发的。

翻车的地方：lmstudio 的 Qwen3.8-27B 有四个 MLX 仓库（4/5/6/8-bit），下载数都在 390 万到 410 万之间，彼此差不到 5%，很像是自动化脚本在拉，所以 MLX 的数字我会打个折看。另外 HF 对 GGUF 是按每个 .gguf 文件的请求来计数的，一个仓库放好几个量化文件就会被重复算，GGUF 偏高是大概率的事。还有，这只是一个时间点的快照，「停滞还是下滑」这种趋势我没法直接验证。

我的判断：决定量化版比例的不是模型有多大，而是它能不能塞进一张消费级显卡或者一台 Mac。太小的原版本来就够轻，没必要量化；太大的量化完也跑不动。如果你要发一个 20B 到 120B 的模型，最好首发当天就自己放出 GGUF 和 MLX 版本，不然大部分用户是从别人那里拿到你的模型的。

Up until a month ago, adaptive verification in vLLM needed a drafter that shipped with a trained confidence head. Now it works with the draft models you already serve: MTP, EAGLE, DFlash, and DSpark checkpoints without a head. No retraining.

The signal was already in the draft logits. The drafter’s own top-token probability ranks drafts as well as a trained confidence head, but it overestimates how often they’ll be accepted. A tiny logistic fit, trained online from the target’s own accept/reject decisions, corrects the calibration.

In our benchmarks, a single adaptive verification config at the max draft length stays on the throughput–interactivity Pareto frontier at most concurrencies, with no per-load tuning. 📈

Available now on main behind enable_adaptive_verification, for draft models whose attention backends support variable-length verification. Built by Giancarlo Delfin @TheEpicDolphin1 (@inferact), on top of adaptive verification by Lucas Wilkinson (@RedHat_AI) and Ben Chislett (@NVIDIAAI).

民主党が上下両院を制し、ホワイトハウス（トランプ政権）と議会が激しく対立する「分割政府（全面グリッドロック）」に突入した場合、市場には「短期的な混乱・ボラティリティの上昇」と「中長期的な財政拡大のブレーキ」という2つの相反する力が働きます。

株式、為替（ドル）、債券市場、そして実体経済への具体的な影響は以下の通りです。

1. 株式市場への影響：セクター別の明暗と乱高下

政策関連銘柄の選別・株価の二極化

恩恵を受けやすいセクター（ヘルスケア・病院関連）: 

民主党主導でオバマケア（ACA）減税措置の延長やメディケイド削減の見直しが動くため、保険・医療サービス関連株には追い風となります。

逆風・不透明感に直面するセクター（防衛・エネルギー）: 

イラン軍事衝突に対する戦争権限決議案や軍備予算の見直し、化石燃料優遇への牽制が入り、防衛産業や伝統的エネルギー株には下押し圧力がかかりやすくなります。

追加法人減税の完全消滅

第1次トランプ減税（TCJA）の恒久化やさらなる法人税引き下げといった共和党主導の追加経済対策は議会で完全に阻止されます。

市場が期待していた「企業優遇の税制拡大シナリオ」は剥落します。

政府閉鎖・債務上限問題による短期ショック

予算審議が期限ぎりぎりまで紛糾し、政府機関の閉鎖（シャットダウン）や債務上限問題が浮上するたびに、VIX指数（恐怖指数）が急上昇し、株価全体が一時的に急落する場面が増加します。

2. 為替市場（ドル）への影響：緩やかな「ドル安」圧力

「トランプ・トレード」の剥落

トランプ大統領の看板政策である包括的な追加関税に対して議会からブレーキがかかる場合、関税によるインフレ再燃シナリオが後退し、金利高・ドル高を支えていた要因が弱まります。

米国債・財政信認の低下による売り

債務上限や予算を巡る激しい党派対立によって、
過去（2011年や2023年など）に見られたような「米国債格下げリスク」が意識されると、
基軸通貨としてのドルに対する信認低下からドル安が進みやすくなります。

FRB（米連邦準備制度理事会）の金融政策

議会の機能不全によって財政出動（景気刺激策）が止まり、経済が冷え込む兆候が出た場合、FRBが利下げに動きやすくなることもドル安要因となります。

3. 債券市場（金利）への影響：国債の乱高下と金利低下バイアス

財政赤字拡大の鈍化（中長期的な金利低下圧力）

両党が互いの看板政策（共和党の大型減税、
民主党の大型社会保障支出）をブロックし合うため、「新たな大盤振る舞いの財政支出が通らない」という状態になります。

これは新規国債の増発ペースを抑える要因となるため、中長期的には米長期金利（10年国債利回り）の低下（債券価格の上昇）につながります。

短期的なスプレッド拡大とボラティリティ

政府閉鎖危機やデフォルト（債務不履行）懸念のニュースが出る局面では、償還期日が近い短期国債が一時的に売られ、短期金利が急騰するなど、イールドカーブ（利回り曲線）の歪みが生じます。

4. 米国経済（実体経済）への影響

企業の設備投資の先送り

関税制度の行方、環境・エネルギー規制、通商方針について政権（大統領令）と議会（阻止法案や訴訟）が真っ向から対立するため、規制の将来予測が極めて難しくなります。

不確実性を嫌う大企業は、大型設備投資や新規雇用の決定を保留・先送りし、実体経済の成長を鈍化させます。

政府閉鎖による一時的なGDP押し下げ

予算不成立により連邦政府機関が一部閉鎖された場合、公務員の給与未払いや行政サービスの停滞が発生し、
四半期ベースのGDP成長率を0.1〜0.5%程度押し下げる直接的な痛手となります
（閉鎖解除後に一部回復するものの、消費マインドを冷え込ませます）。

歴史的に見れば、ウォール街は「大きな政策変更が起きず現状維持が続く」という意味で、ある程度の「分割政府（ねじれ議会）」を好む傾向があります。

しかし、今回は「イラン情勢」「関税権限」「大統領スキャンダルの大規模調査・弾劾」という爆発力の高いテーマが絡んでいるため、単なる立法停滞にとどまらず、突発的な政治リスクが市場を揺さぶる頻度が高くなります。

ICU admissions occurred in 32.7% of patients receiving placebo, compared with just 5.5% receiving ivermectin.

That represents approximately an 83% relative reduction, with an absolute difference of 27.2 percentage points.

Hospital stays were also shorter, with six days reported in the placebo group versus four days in the ivermectin group.

These results deserve scientific attention. But they also need context.

A single small #RandomizedControlledTrial cannot establish that a treatment works across the broader COVID-19 population.

Larger randomized trials, including ACTIV-6, found no clinically meaningful improvement in recovery among outpatients receiving ivermectin.

Those studies involved different patient populations, so direct comparisons require caution.

The 2024 trial also could not demonstrate a mortality benefit or establish long-term safety.

The scientific response should be to examine the methods, compare patient populations and seek independent replication.

Positive findings should not be dismissed automatically.

But they should not be presented as definitive proof that #Ivermectin prevents critical #COVID19.

Reliable treatment evidence depends on results that can be reproduced.

🇨🇳 China’s September PPI rose 5.0% YoY from 3.8%, its highest since June 2022 and above the 4.4% consensus. Exports grew 36.3% YoY and imports 31.0%, both well above expectations. CPI rose just 0.9%, below expectations, and core CPI held at 1.0%.

Oil is pushing up producer prices, but downstream firms are absorbing the cost. PPI rose 1.2% MoM as oil extraction prices jumped 14.5% and refined petroleum prices rose 7.4%. Mining prices climbed 25.4% YoY against 3.4% for processing industries, which means little of the cost is being passed on and downstream margins stay under pressure.

Consumer prices show the same gap. Gasoline rose 16.6% YoY and added about 0.47 percentage points to CPI inflation, more than half the headline increase. Computer and mobile phone prices accelerated to 21.8% and 14.9%. Service prices fell 0.2% MoM after the summer travel season, and food prices rose just 0.4%, below seasonal norms. Price pressure is coming from costs, with little from domestic demand.

Exports are strong, but integrated circuits, automatic data-processing equipment and automobiles made up nearly half of January-September export growth. Integrated circuit export volumes rose just 3.8% while export values surged 108.1%, so higher prices drove much of the gain.

Oil raised import costs too. Crude oil import volumes fell 15.3% YoY in January-September while average prices rose around 18%, leaving import values up just 0.3%.

China still sits between old and new growth drivers, with no broad recovery in domestic demand. A low base should keep PPI inflation elevated near term, but cost-driven inflation is not necessarily positive for corporate earnings when processing industries lack pricing power and face sustained margin pressure. Export growth also leans on AI-related products and partly reflects chip price increases, so external demand is narrower than the headline suggests.

Watch core CPI and service prices for signs of a domestic recovery, and whether upstream cost increases reach end prices.

OpenCode 2.0 is out (Oct 12): a major overhaul of Anomaly's open-source (MIT) coding agent.

- One background service: the TUI, web UI and desktop app now all talk to a single local OpenCode process. Scripts using the new client package auto-discover it, and `opencode pair` connects other apps.
- The server API was rebuilt from scratch, and OpenCode calls its own API, e.g. to move a session into a git worktree.
- Code Mode: a minimal built-in JS interpreter turns MCP servers and OpenAPI endpoints into functions the agent calls from one script. All MCP servers are opted in by default.
- Background subagents (optionally on a different model) and async shell commands. Ctrl+B moves long-running work to the background.
- 80+ features are built as internal plugins, TUI plugins are now stable, and everything hot-reloads.
- A new SDK package ships the same code as the CLI as a library, e.g. for servers or Durable Objects.

Upgrade: get on the latest 1.x, then run `opencode upgrade --major`. Breaking: 1.x plugins don't run, the server API is new, and tui.json config moves to one global cli.json (auto-migrated).

https://t.co/tEYBxbXDnh
